title: Base change and fppf locality of flatness, properness and finite presentation
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], over schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For morphisms of algebraic spaces, flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (the diagonal is quasi-compact). Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; separated means the diagonal is a closed immersion, and universally closed means closed on underlying topological spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Each of the three properties flat, proper, and of finite presentation is preserved by arbitrary base change of algebraic spaces. For a morphism $f:X\to T$ to a scheme and any fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], $f$ has any one of these properties if and only if each $X\times_TT_i\to T_i$ has that property. The assertion is separate for each property; no conjunction of the other two is assumed. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Underlying point sets are field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], with the quotient topology from surjective etale scheme atlases. A quasi-compact space admits a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; a quasi-compact morphism is one whose pullback to any quasi-compact algebraic space has quasi-compact source. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: First record the point-set fact used below. For maps $A\to B\leftarrow C$ of algebraic spaces, representatives $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to A$ and $c:\operatorname{Spec}L\to C$ with the same image in $|B|$ agree over $B$ after a common field extension $M$. Their restrictions therefore define $\operatorname{Spec}M\to A\times_BC$, projecting to the original point classes. Thus $|A\times_BC|\to|A|\times_{|B|}|C|$ is surjective. In particular jointly surjective families remain jointly surjective after every base change. This is a direct use of the definition of point classes and the sheaf fibre-product universal property, not an identification of these two point sets.

Let $P$ be flat, locally of finite presentation, or locally of finite type. Given $f:X\to Y$ with $P$ and $Y'\to Y$, choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme chart $U\to X\times_YV$. The chart test gives $P(U\to V)$. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V'\to Y'\times_YV$. The map $V'\to Y'$ is the composite of $V'\to Y'\times_YV$ and of the base change $Y'\times_YV\to Y'$ of $V\to Y$, both surjective etale; by the chartwise-etale permanence lemma (composites, and agreement with representable etale for a scheme source) and composition of surjections on point classes it is a surjective etale scheme chart of $Y'$, and $U'=U\times_VV'$ is a scheme with a surjective etale map to $X\times_YY'\times_{Y'}V'$. The scheme map $U'\to V'$ is the base change of $U\to V$, so it has $P$ by the corresponding scheme base-change lemma. Apply the chart test again to obtain $P(X\times_YY'\to Y')$. Atlas existence is part of the definition of an algebraic space; preservation of the atlas maps is the etale-cover base-change assertion. Thus this proves arbitrary base-change stability of these three local properties without any hypothesis involving the other two.

Quasi-compactness is stable under arbitrary base change by the quasi-compact-space lemma. If $D=X\times_YX$ and $Y'\to Y$, then $D'= (X\times_YY')\times_{Y'}(X\times_YY')\cong D\times_YY'$; the map $D'\to D$ forgets the common $Y'$ coordinate. Under this isomorphism, $X\times_DD'\cong X\times_YY'$: on any test scheme $W$, a section of the left side consists of $x$ and $((x_1,x_2),y')$ with $(x_1,x_2)=(x,x)$, hence is uniquely a pair $(x,y')$ over $Y$. This correspondence commutes with restriction in $W$ and takes the projection to $D'$ to the new diagonal. Thus the new diagonal is precisely the base change of $\Delta_f:X\to D$ along $D'\to D$. These identities follow by writing the two projections and the single equality over $Y$ in the fibre-product universal property. Hence quasi-compactness of $\Delta_f$ implies quasi-compactness of the new diagonal. Quasi-separatedness is therefore preserved. Combining these two facts with local finite presentation from Step 2 proves preservation of finite presentation. For properness, use the four constituents of the convention of the statement. Finite type is preserved: local finite type by Step 2 and quasi-compactness by the quasi-compact-space lemma. Separatedness is preserved: for a scheme test $Z\to D'$ of the new diagonal, compose with $D'\to D$; pasting fibre squares gives $(X\times_YY')\times_{D'}Z\cong X\times_DZ$ over $Z$, a scheme test of $\Delta_f$, hence a closed immersion. Universal closedness is preserved: for an algebraic-space map $Y''\to Y'$, $(X\times_YY')\times_{Y'}Y''\cong X\times_YY''$ over $Y''$, so the required closedness on $|Y''|$ is an instance of universal closedness of $f$. This proves all three arbitrary base-change assertions.

source.place: Tags 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), 03XR (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation), 04WP (lemma-base-change-proper: combination of the base changes of separated, finite type and universally closed)

proof.text: Every scheme fppf covering in the statement is an fpqc covering in the existing scheme descent lemmas. Indeed, for each affine open $V\subset T$, restrict the covering to $V$ by scheme fppf base change. The affine-refinement lemma supplies finitely many affine opens in the covering schemes whose images cover $V$. The original maps are flat, and these finite affine refinements are exactly the second condition in the definition of an fpqc covering. This applies also to every scheme base change of the original covering.

Now let $T$ be a scheme and suppose all $f_i:X_i=X\times_TT_i\to T_i$ have one fixed local property $P$ among flat, locally of finite presentation, and locally of finite type. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to X$. For each $i$, $U_i=U\times_TT_i$ is a scheme and is a surjective etale atlas of $X_i$. By the chart test with target $T_i$, $U_i\to T_i$ has $P$. The scheme morphism $U\to T$ therefore has $P$ by the appropriate existing fpqc descent lemma and Step 4. The chart test with target $T$ now gives $P(f)$. Each of the three properties is descended separately: the only common flatness/local-presentation hypotheses are those on the covering maps.

source.place: Tags 041W (lemma-descending-property-flat), 041T (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation), 041S (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type): descent on a fixed etale source atlas

proof.text: If all $f_i$ are quasi-compact, the quasi-compact-space lemma immediately gives quasi-compactness of $f$. If all $f_i$ are quasi-separated, put $D=X\times_TX$ and $D_i=D\times_TT_i$. The maps $D_i\to D$ are flat and locally of finite presentation by Step 2 and jointly surjective by Step 1. Moreover $D_i\cong X_i\times_{T_i}X_i$ and $\Delta_{f_i}$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f$ along $D_i\to D$, by the same universal-property calculation as in Step 3. Apply the quasi-compact-space lemma to $\Delta_f$ and this family. The quasi-compactness of every $\Delta_{f_i}$ implies that of $\Delta_f$. Thus quasi-separatedness descends. In particular if all $f_i$ are of finite presentation, Steps 5 and 6 supply respectively local finite presentation and the two quasi-compactness conditions, proving finite presentation of $f$.

To descend separatedness, suppose every $f_i$ is separated. Write $D=X\times_TX$. The relative diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to D$ is the pullback of the representable absolute diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ along $D\to X\times_SX$, with $S$ the common original base scheme. For any scheme test $Z\to D$, the sheaf $E=X\times_DZ$ is therefore $X\times_{X\times_SX}Z$: on sections both consist of $(x,z)$ with the two $X$ coordinates of $z$ equal to $x$. This bijection respects restriction and the projection to $Z$. Thus $E$ is a scheme by representability of the absolute diagonal. The maps $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i\to Z$ form a scheme fppf covering, hence an fpqc covering by Step 4. Each $E\times_ZZ_i\to Z_i$ is a scheme test of $\Delta_{f_i}$, so is a closed immersion. The scheme fpqc descent lemma for closed immersions gives that $E\to Z$ is a closed immersion. Since this holds for every scheme test, $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion and $f$ is separated. This uses the representable meaning of closed immersion; it does not assert that the algebraic space $X$ itself is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0421 (lemma-descending-property-separated), proof by scheme tests of the relative diagonal

proof.text: Suppose every $f_i$ is universally closed. Fix an arbitrary algebraic-space map $T'\to T$ and put $X'=X\times_TT'$, $T_i'=T'\times_TT_i$. The maps $p_i:T_i'\to T'$ are flat and locally of finite presentation by Step 2, jointly surjective by Step 1, and open by the algebraic-space flat-lfp openness lemma. For a closed subset $C\subset|X'|$, let $C_i$ be its inverse image in $|X'\times_{T'}T_i'|$ and let $A$ be its image in $|T'|$. Universal closedness of $f_i$ makes the image $A_i$ of $C_i$ closed in $|T_i'|$. Step 1 gives $A_i=p_i^{-1}(A)$: a pair consisting of a point of $C$ and a point over its image lifts to their fibre product. Consequently each $p_i^{-1}(|T'|\setminus A)$ is open. Its image under the open map $p_i$ is open, and the union of these images is $|T'|\setminus A$ by joint surjectivity. Hence $A$ is closed. This works for every closed $C$ and every $T'$, proving that $f$ is universally closed.

source.place: Tag 041O (lemma-descending-property-universally-closed), closed-image argument; here open fppf maps replace the affine fpqc quotient maps in the source proof

proof.text: Finally assume every $f_i$ is proper. The definition supplies separatedness, quasi-compactness, local finite type and universal closedness of each $f_i$. Steps 5, 6, 7 and 8 give exactly these four properties for $f$. The first two finite-type conditions combine to say that $f$ is of finite type, and hence $f$ is proper. Together with the flatness and finite-presentation descent already obtained in Steps 5 and 6, this proves the reverse implications for all three properties. The forward implications are their arbitrary base-change assertions in Steps 2 and 3. No step assumes that $f$ is flat in the proper case, or that $f$ is proper in the flat or finite-presentation cases.

lean.statement: theorem flat_proper_fp_locality {S : Scheme.{u}} (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpace S)) (hP : P = @MapIsFlat S ∨ P = @MapIsProper S ∨ P = fun _ _ f ↦ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) : (∀ {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y), P f → P (enlargedFibreProductFst g f)) ∧ (∀ {I : Type w} (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i : I ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i : I ↦ (g i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left → (P f ↔ ∀ i : I, P (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map (g i)⟩ : schemeSpace (Tᵢ i) ⟶ schemeSpace T) f)))
lean.note: The property parameter selects flatness, properness or the explicit conjunction defining finite presentation, separately. First conjunct: arbitrary algebraic-space base change. Second conjunct: equivalence for every scheme fppf covering. Reuses the landed chartwise morphism predicates and affine-test quasi-compactness, equivalent to the stated quasi-compact-space tests; no additional definition or statement correction.
